newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 1997 coffee output seen down 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 1997 coffee output seen down 30 pct.

text.p: Indonesia's 1997 coffee production is expected to be some 30 percent short of an originally forecast 480,000 tonnes due to bad weather, the chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters (AICE), Oesman Soedargo, said on Monday.

"Surveys done by exporters showed that incessant rains in 1996 and strong winds in coffee-growing areas in Sumatra had affected the fruiting process resulting in a decline in coffee production," he said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
He said results of the survey were received three days ago, and that the exportable volume would amount to some 220,000 tonnes this year, compared with about 300,000 tonnes in 1996.

Soedargo said domestic consumption would total about 120,000 tonnes this year, while carry over stocks would total 20,000 tonnes. "The exportable volume from this year's crop would only be 220,000 tonnes," he said.

He also expressed concern over the possibility that there might not be much coffee left for exports in the first and second quarters of the 1997/98 (October/September) crop year because of the decline in production and on-going exports.
Indonesia is the world's third largest coffee producer after Brazil and Colombia.
